turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I'm baking a two-layer chocolate sponge for my nephew's birthday on Sunday and it has to be completely dairy-free. I've got a 20cm round tin and a 23cm round tin. How much batter does each one hold?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Dairy-free is no trouble; use a hard block margarine, not a soft spread. The 20cm holds about 700ml and the 23cm about a litre, and don't fill either tin past two thirds of the way up. Can you say that back to me?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Don't fill either tin past two thirds of the way up. I'll do a double batch so I get two layers.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: A double batch gives you two even layers. Line the base with parchment and grease the sides with a little of the margarine.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Will do. I'll get the tin lined and greased tonight so Sunday is only mixing and baking.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Then Sunday is only the fun part. Bring the eggs out of the fridge the night before as well, because cold eggs curdle the mix.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Eggs out on Saturday night, then. The candles and the cake board are already sorted.
